title: Micah Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Micah chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Micah Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Micah Chapter 3.

questions.question: To whom does Micah address his plea to hear about judgment?
options: Heads of Jacob and princes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Heads of Jacob and princes of Israel
questions.explanation: Micah 3:1 directly addresses the 'heads of Jacob' and 'princes of the house of Israel' as those who should know judgment.

questions.question: According to Micah 3:2, what do the leaders hate and love?
options: Hate the good, love the evil
Hate the evil, love the good
Hate the poor, love the rich
questions.correctAnswer: Hate the good, love the evil
questions.explanation: Micah 3:2 states that the leaders hate the good and love the evil.

questions.question: What cruel actions are described in Micah 3:3 as being done to God's people?
options: Eating their flesh and flaying their skin
questions.correctAnswer: Eating their flesh and flaying their skin
questions.explanation: Micah 3:3 describes how the leaders 'eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them;'

questions.question: What will happen when the people cry unto the LORD according to Micah 3:4?
options: The LORD will not hear them and will hide His face
The LORD will send an angel
The LORD will bless them abundantly
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will not hear them and will hide His face
questions.explanation: Micah 3:4 says that when they cry unto the LORD, He will not hear them and will hide His face because of their ill behavior.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets in Micah 3 bite with their teeth and cry 'Peace'.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 3:5 states that the prophets 'bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace'.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 3:6 promises that the prophets will have visions and divine clearly.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 3:6 says that 'night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision' and that 'the day shall be dark over them,' indicating no clear divine guidance.

questions.question: Who shall be ashamed and cover their lips because there is no answer of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Seers and diviners
questions.explanation: Micah 3:7 states that the seers shall be ashamed and the diviners confounded and will cover their lips for there is no answer of God.

questions.question: According to Micah 3:8, what is Micah filled with by the spirit of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Power, judgment, and might
questions.explanation: Micah 3:8 says Micah is full of power by the spirit of the LORD, and of judgment, and of might.

questions.question: Who does Micah call out for abhorring judgment and perverting equity?
options: Heads of the house of Jacob and princes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Heads of the house of Jacob and princes of Israel
questions.explanation: Micah 3:9 addresses the heads of the house of Jacob and princes of Israel who abhor judgment and pervert equity.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 3:10, Zion and Jerusalem are built up with peace and righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 3:10 states that Zion is built up with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity, not peace and righteousness.

questions.question: According to Micah 3:11, what motivates the heads, priests, and prophets in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Reward, hire, and money
questions.explanation: Micah 3:11 describes how the heads judge for reward, priests teach for hire, and prophets divine for money.

questions.question: What false confidence do the leaders have according to Micah 3:11?
options: They lean upon the LORD saying no evil can come upon them
They trust in their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: They lean upon the LORD saying no evil can come upon them
questions.explanation: Micah 3:11 says they 'lean upon the LORD, and say, Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us.'

questions.question: What will happen to Zion and Jerusalem for the leaders' sake, according to Micah 3:12?
options: Zion will be plowed as a field and Jerusalem become heaps
They will be glorified and prosper
They will be defended by angels
They will be rebuilt with gold
questions.correctAnswer: Zion will be plowed as a field and Jerusalem become heaps
questions.explanation: Micah 3:12 declares that Zion shall be plowed as a field and Jerusalem become heaps due to the leaders' sins.

questions.question: Which comes first in Micah 3: the leaders hating the good or the LORD hiding His face?
options: Leaders hating the good comes first
The LORD hiding His face comes first
Both happen at the same time
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders hating the good comes first
questions.explanation: Micah 3:2 describes the leaders hating the good, and Micah 3:4 explains that the LORD will then hide His face.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 3 describes the leaders as caring for the well-being of the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 3:2-3 shows leaders harming the people by hating good and eating their flesh, indicating they do not care for their well-being.

medium.title: Micah Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Micah Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Micah 3:5, how do the false prophets cause harm to God's people?
options: They make the people err and cry 'Peace' deceitfully
They lead the people in worship of idols
They refuse to speak at all
They encourage the people to fast and pray
questions.correctAnswer: They make the people err and cry 'Peace' deceitfully
questions.explanation: Micah 3:5 states that the prophets make the people err, biting with their teeth and crying 'Peace', which is deceptive. This shows their harmful influence contrasting true prophecy.

questions.question: What consequence does Micah 3:6 say will come upon the prophets because of their falsehood?
options: They will be given true visions
Night and darkness will come upon them, preventing them from seeing visions
They will be honored among the people
They will receive wealth and power
questions.correctAnswer: Night and darkness will come upon them, preventing them from seeing visions
questions.explanation: Micah 3:6 clearly states that night and darkness will be upon the prophets so they will not have visions or divine, indicating God's judgment on their false prophecy.

questions.question: How does Micah 3:7 describe the reaction of seers and diviners when God does not answer them?
options: They are ashamed and cover their lips
questions.correctAnswer: They are ashamed and cover their lips
questions.explanation: Verse 7 explains that seers will be ashamed and diviners confounded, covering their lips because there is no answer from God, showing their impotence without divine guidance.

questions.question: What does Micah 3:8 reveal about the prophet's source of power to declare sin and transgression?
options: Power from the spirit of the LORD
Power from wisdom gained by study
questions.correctAnswer: Power from the spirit of the LORD
questions.explanation: Micah 3:8 shows that the true prophet is empowered by the Spirit of the LORD to declare Jacob's transgression and Israel's sin, contrasting false prophets who lack this divine empowerment.

questions.question: Based on Micah 3:5-6, what will happen to those who try to prophesy falsely and deceive the people?
options: They will gain great respect and influence
They will be unable to receive visions and will live in darkness
They will be rewarded with wealth
They will be supported by all the people
questions.correctAnswer: They will be unable to receive visions and will live in darkness
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes false prophecy causing error, and verse 6 warns that such prophets will be given darkness instead of visions, illustrating that falsehood leads to spiritual blindness.

questions.question: How does Micah 3:7-8 illustrate the difference between false prophets and the true prophet?
options: False prophets are ashamed due to no answer; true prophet is empowered by God's spirit
Both false and true prophets receive visions equally
False prophets gain wealth; true prophet seeks peace
False prophets are silent; true prophet is silent too
questions.correctAnswer: False prophets are ashamed due to no answer; true prophet is empowered by God's spirit
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 contrast false seers ashamed without answers and the true prophet filled with the Spirit of the LORD to declare sin and judgment.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can a Christian learn from the false prophets described in Micah 3:5-7?
options: Integrity requires honesty and reliance on God's Spirit, not deceit
Integrity means pleasing everyone at all costs
Integrity is about gaining power and money
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity requires honesty and reliance on God's Spirit, not deceit
questions.explanation: Micah 3:5-7 condemns deceitful prophets who mislead and receive no answer from God, teaching believers the importance of honest, Spirit-guided speech.

questions.question: According to Micah 3:8, how is the Spirit of the LORD involved in proclaiming sin and transgression?
options: It empowers the prophet with power, judgment, and might
It provides wisdom for worldly success
It grants visions unrelated to sin
questions.correctAnswer: It empowers the prophet with power, judgment, and might
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states the prophet is full of power by the Spirit of the LORD to declare sin and judgment, showing the Spirit's essential role in true prophetic ministry.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles with discouragement because their prayers seem unanswered, similar to the seers in Micah 3:7. Based on this passage, what biblical truth should encourage them?
options: True answers come from God’s Spirit, not from deceitful words
questions.correctAnswer: True answers come from God’s Spirit, not from deceitful words
questions.explanation: Micah 3:7 shows false prophets receive no answer and are ashamed, while verse 8 reveals true prophecy is empowered by God’s Spirit, encouraging trust in God’s genuine guidance.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 3:6 promises that false prophets will be able to divine the future despite their deceitful ways.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 3:6 states the sun will go down over the prophets and the day will be dark for them, meaning they will not have visions or be able to divine, showing God’s judgment on false prophecy.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 3:9-10 condemns leaders who pervert justice and build Jerusalem with blood and iniquity.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 9 rebukes leaders for abhorring judgment and perverting equity, and verse 10 condemns building Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity, highlighting corrupt leadership.

questions.question: What does Micah 3:11 reveal about the motives of heads, priests, and prophets in Jerusalem?
options: They judge, teach, and divine for reward and money
They fast and pray for the people
questions.correctAnswer: They judge, teach, and divine for reward and money
questions.explanation: Micah 3:11 states the leaders and priests judge and teach for hire, and prophets divine for money, showing their corrupt motives despite trusting in the LORD’s presence.

questions.question: How does Micah 3:12 describe the consequence for Zion and Jerusalem due to the leaders' corruption?
options: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become heaps
Jerusalem will be a place of peace forever
The mountain of the house will be rebuilt
questions.correctAnswer: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become heaps
questions.explanation: Verse 12 predicts Zion will be destroyed like a field plowed and Jerusalem reduced to heaps because of the leaders’ wrongdoing, signaling God’s judgment.

questions.question: What does Micah 3:4 warn will happen when people cry unto the LORD after behaving ill in their deeds?
options: The LORD will hide His face and not hear them
The LORD will immediately answer their prayers
The LORD will send angels to help
The LORD will forgive without condition
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will hide His face and not hear them
questions.explanation: Verse 4 warns that when those who have behaved ill cry unto the LORD, He will not hear them but hide His face, showing the consequences of persistent evil deeds.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 3:1, it is the responsibility of the heads of Jacob and princes of Israel to know judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 3:1 addresses the heads of Jacob and princes of Israel, stating it is their role to know judgment, highlighting their leadership responsibility.

hard.title: Micah Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Micah Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who does Micah address as those who abhor judgment and pervert all equity?
options: Heads of the house of Jacob and princes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Heads of the house of Jacob and princes of Israel
questions.explanation: Micah 3:9 specifically addresses the heads of the house of Jacob and princes of Israel as those who abhor judgment and pervert equity.

questions.question: According to Micah 3, what do the leaders build up Zion and Jerusalem with?
questions.correctAnswer: Blood and iniquity
questions.explanation: Micah 3:10 states that the leaders build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity, indicating corruption and violence under their rule.

questions.question: What corrupt practices do the heads, priests, and prophets engage in according to Micah 3:11?
options: Judging for reward, teaching for hire, and divining for money
questions.correctAnswer: Judging for reward, teaching for hire, and divining for money
questions.explanation: Micah 3:11 condemns the leaders for judging, teaching, and prophesying for personal gain rather than for justice.

questions.question: Despite their corruption, what false confidence do the leaders express?
options: Is not the LORD among us? None evil can come upon us.
We will build a temple greater than Solomon's.
The people love us and obey our commands.
God has forsaken us and left us to perish.
questions.correctAnswer: Is not the LORD among us? None evil can come upon us.
questions.explanation: The leaders falsely rely on God's presence as a guarantee of safety despite their unjust actions, as stated in Micah 3:11.

questions.question: What is the consequence for Zion and Jerusalem because of the leaders' wrongdoing?
options: Zion will be plowed as a field and Jerusalem become heaps
They will be exalted and prosper
They will rebuild the temple in glory
They will be blessed with peace and abundance
questions.correctAnswer: Zion will be plowed as a field and Jerusalem become heaps
questions.explanation: Micah 3:12 foretells the destruction of Zion and Jerusalem as a direct result of the leaders' sinful actions.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly warns against leaders who judge for reward and priests who teach for hire, echoing Micah 3?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 1:23
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:23 similarly condemns leaders who judge for reward and priests who teach for hire, paralleling the condemnation in Micah 3:11.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of false prophets who mislead people, as seen in Micah 3:5?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Peter 2:1-3
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:1-3 warns about false teachers who deceive and exploit people, echoing the theme of false prophets in Micah 3:5.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Micah 3:2-3, where the leaders are described as plucking off skin and breaking bones?
questions.correctAnswer: Graphic imagery and metaphor
questions.explanation: Micah 3:2-3 uses graphic imagery and metaphor to depict the cruelty and exploitation of the leaders toward the people.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'judge' (שָׁפַט, shaphat) imply in the context of Micah 3:9?
questions.correctAnswer: To govern or administer justice
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root שָׁפַט (shaphat) used in Micah 3:9 refers to governing or administering justice, highlighting the leaders' failure in this role.

questions.question: According to Micah 3:6-7, what happens to the seers and diviners when God hides His face?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 3:6-7 explains that when God hides His face, the seers and diviners are ashamed and confounded, unable to provide answers.

questions.question: The leaders in Micah 3 claim that because the LORD is among them, no evil can come upon them. This reflects a true understanding of God's protection.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 3:11 shows the leaders' false confidence in God's presence, while verse 12 warns of coming destruction due to their sins.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the mountain of the house' becoming like the high places of the forest in Micah 3:12?
options: It symbolizes the destruction and desecration of the temple mount
It indicates a future flourishing of the temple
It refers to the building of new altars
It describes a literal forest growing around the mountain
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the destruction and desecration of the temple mount
questions.explanation: Micah 3:12 uses this phrase to symbolize the ruin and desolation of the temple mount, comparing it to wild, uncultivated high places.

questions.question: How does Micah 3:8 demonstrate the prophet's authority to speak against Israel's sin?
options: He is filled with power by the spirit of the LORD to declare transgression and sin
He is elected by the people to lead
He receives messages from foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: He is filled with power by the spirit of the LORD to declare transgression and sin
questions.explanation: Micah 3:8 declares that the prophet's authority comes from the power of the LORD's spirit to expose sin in Israel.

questions.question: Micah 3:4 warns that when the leaders cry to the LORD, He will not hear them. What Old Testament principle does this illustrate?
options: God's immediate forgiveness for all prayers
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment on persistent disobedience
questions.explanation: Micah 3:4 illustrates the principle that God hides His face and does not hear prayers when people persistently behave wickedly.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a prophecy about Jerusalem's destruction that parallels Micah 3:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 26
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26 also prophesies Jerusalem's destruction, paralleling the themes of judgment found in Micah 3:12.

theological.title: Micah Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Micah Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Micah call the heads of Jacob and the princes of Israel to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Know judgment
questions.explanation: Micah urges the leaders to know judgment, emphasizing their responsibility for justice (Micah 3:1).

questions.question: According to Micah, what do the leaders of Israel love?
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: The leaders are described as those who hate the good and love the evil (Micah 3:2).

questions.question: How does Micah describe the actions of those who oppress the people?
options: They eat the flesh of my people
questions.correctAnswer: They eat the flesh of my people
questions.explanation: Micah vividly describes the brutality of oppressors who consume the flesh of the people (Micah 3:3).

questions.question: What will happen when the leaders cry out to the LORD?
options: He will hide His face from them
questions.correctAnswer: He will hide His face from them
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will not hear them and will hide His face due to their ill behavior (Micah 3:4).

questions.question: What do the prophets do, according to Micah?
questions.correctAnswer: Make my people err
questions.explanation: The LORD condemns the prophets for leading the people astray (Micah 3:5).

questions.question: What will happen to the prophets and seers according to Micah?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be ashamed
questions.explanation: The seers will be ashamed and the diviners confounded due to the absence of God's response (Micah 3:7).

questions.question: What power does Micah claim to have?
options: Power by the spirit of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Power by the spirit of the LORD
questions.explanation: Micah states he is full of power by the spirit of the LORD to declare Israel's sin (Micah 3:8).

questions.question: What do the heads of Jacob abhor?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment
questions.explanation: Micah accuses the leaders of abominating judgment and perverting equity (Micah 3:9).

questions.question: What is said about how the leaders build up Zion?
questions.correctAnswer: With blood
questions.explanation: They build up Zion with blood, indicating corruption and violence (Micah 3:10).

questions.question: What do the priests do for hire according to Micah?
questions.correctAnswer: Teach for hire
questions.explanation: Micah condemns the priests for teaching for personal gain (Micah 3:11).

questions.question: What do the leaders mistakenly believe about the LORD's presence?
options: None evil can come upon us
questions.correctAnswer: None evil can come upon us
questions.explanation: Despite their corruption, the leaders falsely assure themselves that no evil can come upon them because of the LORD's presence (Micah 3:11).

questions.question: What will happen to Zion because of the leaders' actions?
options: It will be plowed as a field
questions.correctAnswer: It will be plowed as a field
questions.explanation: Micah prophesies that Zion will be plowed because of the leaders' wrongdoing (Micah 3:12).

questions.question: How does Micah 3:8 connect to the concept of judgment in the chapter?
options: It illustrates divine power for judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates divine power for judgment
questions.explanation: Micah's declaration of being full of power by the Spirit indicates God's authority to judge Israel's sins (Micah 3:8).

questions.question: What does Micah 3:5-6 reveal about the role of false prophets?
options: They lead the people to peace
They create confusion and lead to darkness
questions.correctAnswer: They create confusion and lead to darkness
questions.explanation: The false prophets lead the people astray, resulting in a lack of vision and divine guidance (Micah 3:5-6).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about social justice. What does Micah 3:1-12 actually teach?
questions.correctAnswer: God demands justice from leaders
questions.explanation: Micah's indictment of leaders for their unjust actions shows that God deeply cares about justice and righteousness in society (Micah 3:1-12).
